analysis:
The change is documentation-only in docs/architecture/inference.md: the 'Last updated' date moves to 2026-10-28 (line 3), and one paragraph at about line 1293 gains a description of `PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup`. That description says lookup snapshots all of a request's hits before promoting them between two bounded generations, so a rotation mid-lookup cannot turn a later piece into a miss. It also says token arrays share storage during the snapshot, the existing admission and byte bounds still apply, and batches with no old-generation hits skip the promotion pass.

No code, protocol, key-handling or authorization behavior is changed by this patch. Relevant threat entries are T-041 (prefix-cache and TTFT oracle) and T-028 (residual data). The paragraph states that reuse never crosses a prefix-cache scope. That matches the coordinator-authored cacheSalt scoping in T-041, and the documentation does not weaken or contradict it. The described snapshot only affects cache-hit consistency, and it states that bounds are unchanged, so it introduces no new disclosure or availability assumption.

The prompt-piece token cache holds token IDs in process memory only. It is not an at-rest artifact, so the T-041 SSD at-rest posture (HMAC names, 30-minute TTL, AAD) is untouched.

Remaining question for integration: the actual implementation of `PromptPieceTokenStore` is not in the supplied evidence. The claims that scope isolation holds across the snapshot and that bounds are preserved are therefore unverified. A future code PR should confirm that shared-storage snapshots cannot leak token arrays across cache scopes. Only documentation was reviewed here, so no regression is found.
